1Purpose

This policy is the frame for the module at [Provider name]. It names the seven standards we work to and the policy that carries each one, the roles that run the module, and the rules that apply across the whole module. It sets no time limit and restates no commitment of its own: each of POL-ECS-02 to POL-ECS-08 holds its commitments, its clocks and its checks in one place. It is for families, our workers, the other services in a child's team, and the people who check our work.

2Applies to

  • Every child who receives early childhood supports from us, and their , from first contact until supports end.
  • Everyone who works for [Provider name] and has contact with those children or families: employees, contractors, students, volunteers and key personnel.
  • Every place we work: the family home, early learning and school settings, community places, our premises, and phone or video sessions.
  • A sole trader or partnership registered for these supports, in the same way as a larger provider.

This policy is the shared frame for the module. POL-ECS-02 to POL-ECS-08 each set out one standard in full, with its own commitments, times and checks; nothing in this policy changes them. POL-CHS-01 Child Safe Policy sets the child safety rules for all our work with children; until it is written, the appendix to POL-ECS-02 holds the state and territory reporting schedule.

3Commitments

C1

We will do what POL-ECS-02 The Child Policy (Early Childhood Supports) commits to (the child, s 56).

C2

We will do what POL-ECS-03 The Family Policy (Early Childhood Supports) commits to (the family, s 57).

C3

We will do what POL-ECS-04 Inclusion Policy (Early Childhood Supports) commits to (inclusion, s 58).

C4

We will do what POL-ECS-05 Collaboration Policy (Early Childhood Supports) commits to (collaboration, s 59).

C5

We will do what POL-ECS-06 Capacity Building Policy (Early Childhood Supports) commits to (capacity building, s 60).

C6

We will do what POL-ECS-07 Evidence-Informed Practice Policy (Early Childhood Supports) commits to (evidence-informed supports, s 61).

C7

We will do what POL-ECS-08 Outcome Based Approach Policy (Early Childhood Supports) commits to (outcome based approach, s 62).

4Ground rules

G1

A child's safety comes before everything else in this policy. A worker who is worried about a child acts on that worry first.

G2

A person with decides about the child's supports. We ask for the child's own views in a way that fits their age and how they communicate, and we record them.

G3

One route for every concern. A practice concern goes to the . A conduct or safety concern about a colleague or a manager goes to the Chief Executive. A concern about the Chief Executive or an owner goes to the chair of the governing body, or in a sole trader's business to the independent contact named in REG-GOV-01 Delegations Register. A child who may be at goes to the the same day, under PRO-ECS-02 The Child Procedure (Early Childhood Supports). The person a concern is about never handles it.

G4

The time limits of the module are set in POL-ECS-02 to POL-ECS-08 and the procedures under them; the Module clocks table at the end of these ground rules reproduces them, and this policy sets none of its own. Where the law sets a shorter time, the shorter time applies.

G5

The appendix to POL-ECS-02 holds the state and territory reporting schedule: the law of [state or territory] on who must report, the test, where, how fast, and the duty of every adult to tell police of child sexual abuse. POL-CHS-01, when written, holds the wider child safe standards and reportable conduct rules. The Quality Manager checks the schedule every 12 months and when the law changes.

G6

Each fact is held once. REG-ECS-01 Early Childhood Supports Register is the one register for the module and holds dates, names, counts and record numbers. The forms hold the detail and the family's words.

G7

A family can say no to a , a referral, a team meeting or a question. Saying no is recorded and is never a reason to reduce supports.

G8

A complaint made by a child or family at any point is handled under PRO-FBK-01 Feedback and Complaints Management Procedure. A child's "stop" or "not happy" signal is a complaint the child can make in their own way.

G9

A sole trader holds every role except practice supervisor and independent contact for concerns. An outside practice supervisor with early childhood experience and the independent contact named in REG-GOV-01 Delegations Register are the checks on the sole trader's own work.

G10

The is the accountable for the child's plan and the register row. Where the family chooses a key worker from our team, the key worker is the plan lead, and when the key worker changes the plan-lead role moves with it the same day.

345 words
early childhood supports
supports for a young child with developmental delay or disability, and their family, under the registration class "early intervention supports for early childhood".
family
the parents, carers and other people who raise the child, as the family itself describes them.
parental responsibility
the legal authority to make decisions for a child. A court or child protection order can change who holds it.
support network
the relatives, friends, educators and others in the child's everyday life whom the family chooses to involve.
everyday routines
the things the child does most days, such as meals, play, bath time, getting dressed and going to early learning.
key worker
the one practitioner the family chooses as their main contact. Where the family chooses a key worker, that person is the plan lead.
team around the child
the family, our practitioners and the other providers who work together on the child's plan.
plan lead
the practitioner accountable for the child's plan and the register row.
practice supervisor
the clinical supervisor of the early childhood practitioners.
practitioner drafting for the plan lead
the practitioner the plan lead asks to draft the plan under PRO-ECS-08. The plan lead stays accountable for the plan.
functional outcome
something the child will do in daily life, written so the family can see when it has happened.
coaching
helping a parent, carer or educator practise a strategy in their own routine, in place of doing it for them.
both clearances
an NDIS worker screening clearance, and the working with children check of [state or territory].
child safety lead
the role the Chief Executive names to receive every concern about a child and to see that reports are made.
risk of harm
the words this module uses for the reporting threshold. Our test is that you suspect on reasonable grounds that a child is at risk of harm. The appendix to POL-ECS-02 gives the exact term used in [state or territory].
business day
a day other than a Saturday, a Sunday or a public holiday in the state or territory where the participant lives.

docs.html:
1Purpose

[Provider name] uses strategies that rest on stated principles and the best available evidence. Our choose strategies within their and with the , write down what each one rests on, and keep their skills current. This policy is for families, our practitioners and the people who check our work.

2Applies to

  • Every child who receives from us, and their family.
  • Every we use or recommend: an approach, a programme, a technique, an assessment tool, an outcome measure or a piece of equipment.
  • Every practitioner and manager of ours who delivers, plans or oversees early childhood supports. This covers employees, contractors, students and volunteers.
  • Every setting: the family home, early learning, school, the community, our premises, and phone or video.

A student or volunteer follows this policy with a practitioner watching. This policy does not bind other providers. It sets how we check what we use with them.

3Commitments

C1

We will use only strategies that rest on stated principles and the best available evidence. A practitioner chooses a strategy within their professional scope. Before they first use it with a child, they make a short entry on FRM-ECS-06 Section C: the principle it rests on, one or two sources or the practice wisdom and family preference it draws on, any risk or legal limit, and who may deliver it. The adds it to the one-page within 10 of the entry. A strategy is not held back while it is listed, unless it fails the restraint or law questions.

Answers: Legislation (1). How we do it: Procedure step 3, Procedure step 4, Procedure step 5, Procedure step 9, Procedure step 10, Procedure step 12.

C2

We will never bar a strategy only because it has no published evidence. Where the evidence is limited, the practitioner's reasoning and the family's preference may support its use as a , with the outcome's measure in the child's plan and a look at the next progress check. We do not use a strategy shown to harm, or shown not to work for children like this one. We write the in words, never as a letter grade.

Answers: Legislation (1). How we do it: Procedure step 6, Procedure step 9.

C3

We will not use a strategy that restrains, secludes or confines a child, or that breaks a law that applies to it. Every answers the restraint and law questions before the strategy is used.

Answers: Legislation (1). How we do it: Procedure step 7, Procedure step 9.

C4

We will have the Practice supervisor review the strategy list every 3 months. The Practice supervisor may ask for a change: another source, a limit, a measure, or that a strategy stops. We also review a strategy within 20 business days of learning of new evidence that could change its use. If new evidence shows a strategy may harm a child, we stop it the same day.

Answers: Legislation (1). How we do it: Procedure step 2, Procedure step 27, Procedure step 28.

C5

We will tell each family what the evidence says, in plain words and before they agree. We say how sure we are, what the strategy asks of them and what else they could choose, and we record their decision on the child's plan. If a family asks for a strategy that is not on our list, the practitioner makes the entry the same way, and we give the family our answer within 20 business days.

Answers: Legislation (1), Legislation (2). How we do it: Procedure step 8, Procedure step 13.

C6

We will check every handout, picture guide and video against the strategy entry before we give it out, and again at the quarterly review of the list.

Answers: Legislation (2). How we do it: Procedure step 8, Procedure step 9.

C7

We will let a registered or certified practitioner deliver a strategy within their professional scope without a separate . A per-practitioner sign-off, given after a qualified practitioner has watched at least 2 sessions, is needed only for a : eating, drinking, swallowing, medicine or a health procedure. A practitioner may deliver another discipline's strategy () when the qualified practitioner has written on the strategy list what is released, has shown it, and reviews it at a set interval. Medicine and health procedures are never released.

Answers: Legislation (2). How we do it: Procedure step 11, Procedure step 12.

C8

We will give each practitioner the information and expertise to support the child and the people in the child's life. Each can reach the National Best Practice Framework for Early Childhood Intervention (2025), the evidence for our strategies and a named expert to ask. If nobody we can reach has the expertise a child needs, we tell the family and refer or take advice.

Answers: Legislation (2). How we do it: Procedure step 2, Procedure step 14.

C9

We will give each practitioner with the Practice supervisor at least every 3 months. Each one ends with one agreed change to practice.

Answers: Legislation (3). How we do it: Procedure step 1, Procedure step 18, Procedure step 19.

C10

We will have each practitioner assess their own practice against best practice within 60 business days of starting, and every 12 months. Every rating needs an example from a record; a new starter may use an example from a previous role, with no child's name. The Practice supervisor reviews it within 10 business days and agrees up to 3 goals.

Answers: Legislation (3). How we do it: Procedure step 15, Procedure step 16, Procedure step 25.

C11

We will arrange a of each practitioner's practice at least every 6 months. The peer watches a session with the family's agreement, reads 2 session records or talks through a case with no names. The peer gives feedback within 5 business days. For a sole trader, a case discussion with the outside clinical supervisor is the peer review.

Answers: Legislation (3). How we do it: Procedure step 21, Procedure step 22.

C12

We will plan and record each practitioner's . Each completes the hours their professional standard sets (the Board's standard for a registered profession, Speech Pathology Australia's for speech pathology, the teacher registration body's for an early childhood teacher), and at least 20 hours in each 12 months, pro rata, where the profession sets none. At least half is on early childhood intervention practice. We count hours as the practitioner's professional standard counts them. We check within 3 months whether practice changed.

Answers: Legislation (3). How we do it: Procedure step 17, Procedure step 23, Procedure step 24, Procedure step 25, Procedure step 26.

C13

We will monitor our practice against what happens for children. Every 3 months the Practice supervisor's one quarterly read covers two plans of each practitioner against the strategy list and the outcomes, together with their session records under POL-ECS-06 Capacity Building Policy (Early Childhood Supports). Every 6 months the Quality Manager reports what the results show in the one early childhood quality report covering sections 56 to 62.

Answers: Legislation (1), Legislation (3). How we do it: Procedure step 20, Procedure step 30.

C14

We will stop at once any use of a strategy that fails the restraint or law questions, and any health-related practice outside a worker's qualification or sign-off. The Practice supervisor looks into each concern within 5 business days. Nobody is disadvantaged for raising a concern.

Answers: Legislation (1), Legislation (2). How we do it: Procedure step 29.

4Ground rules

G1

We weigh three things together: the best available research, the practitioner's skill, and what the child and family value and choose. None decides alone.

G2

Every strategy follows six principles, drawn from the National Best Practice Framework for Early Childhood Intervention (2025). Principle 1: the family leads. They know their child best and make the decisions. Principle 2: learning happens in , in the places the child lives, learns and plays. Principle 3: we build the skills and confidence of the people around the child. Principle 4: we start from the strengths of the child and the family. Principle 5: we work as one team, with the family at the centre. Principle 6: the child's rights, voice and safety come first. A strategy that cannot follow principle 1 or 6 is never used.

G3

A family can say no to any strategy, rating, recording or peer watching a session. Saying no never reduces supports.

G4

No strategy of ours may restrain, seclude or confine a child, or limit what they can reach or use in order to change their behaviour. If a child's behaviour seems to need one, the Service Manager is told the same day and gets specialist behaviour support advice.

G5

A health-related strategy (eating, drinking, swallowing, medicine or any health procedure) is used only by a practitioner qualified and signed off for it. G6

A source written, funded or sold by the maker or seller of a strategy needs a second source with no link to them. A testimonial or a website alone is not a source.

G7

A child's name never goes into a , a peer review or a group learning session. We use the child's record number. We share a child's information only as the family's consent allows.

G8

Reflection, and peer review are for learning. A rating or a reflection is never, by itself, a reason for discipline. We act at once if a record shows a child at risk, or work outside a qualification.

G9

A concern about how a colleague practises goes to the Practice supervisor. A concern about a colleague's conduct towards a child or family, or about safety, or about the Practice supervisor, goes to the Chief Executive; a concern about the Chief Executive goes to the chair of the governing body. A sole trader's concern goes to the independent contact named in REG-GOV-01 Delegations Register. strategy
any approach, programme, technique, assessment tool, outcome measure or piece of equipment that we use or recommend to a child or family.
evidence entry
the short written entry for one strategy, in Section C of FRM-ECS-06. It covers the principle, the evidence basis, the risks, the legal limits, who may deliver it and the family summary.
evidence basis
what a strategy rests on, written in words: a current framework or guideline; a review or study; limited or early evidence; or practice wisdom and the family's preference with no harm signal. A strategy shown to harm, or shown not to work for children like this one, has no basis and is not used.
monitored trial
use of a strategy whose evidence basis is limited or rests on practice wisdom and family preference, with the family's agreement, the outcome's measure in the plan and a look at the next progress check.
strategy list
the one-page list of every strategy we use, with its number, principle, evidence basis, who may deliver it, any limit or role release, and its last quarterly review. The Practice supervisor keeps it in the practice file until a Rise strategy register exists.
family summary
what we tell a family about a strategy, in plain words. It covers what the strategy is, what it asks of them and what the evidence says. It also says how sure we are, what else they could choose, and any risk or cost.
best practice framework
the National Best Practice Framework for Early Childhood Intervention (2025), or the later edition listed in REG-GOV-03.
sign-off
the Practice supervisor's written confirmation that a practitioner may deliver a health-related strategy on their own. Other strategies need no sign-off; the practitioner's professional scope covers them.

what a practitioner's registration or certification and their training let them do. The practitioner and the Practice supervisor write its limits at FRM-ECS-06 question 3.

health-related strategy

practice file
the place where the Practice supervisor keeps each practitioner's practice record and what supports it.

a colleague with no authority over the practitioner watches a session, reads two session records or talks through a case, then gives feedback.
professional development
learning that builds a practitioner's skills and knowledge, such as courses, reading with notes, mentoring and learning groups. Supervision and peer review time count only where the practitioner's professional standard counts them.
practitioner
a worker of ours who delivers or plans early childhood supports.

the clinical supervisor of the early childhood practitioners. In a small provider, one outside clinical supervisor with early childhood experience.

the practitioner accountable for the child's plan and the register row.
key worker
the one practitioner the family chooses as their main contact. Where the family chooses a key worker of ours, that person is the plan lead.

the role the Chief Executive names to receive every concern about a child and to see that reports are made.

the relatives, friends, educators and providers in the child's everyday life whom the family chooses to involve.

docs.html:
1Purpose

The result: every we use with a child rests on stated principles and the best available evidence, written down before it is used. The law allows it, and a working within their delivers it; a is delivered only by a practitioner signed off for it. Each practitioner's skills stay current through reflection, , and planned learning.

This procedure gives effect to POL-ECS-07 Evidence-Informed Practice Policy (Early Childhood Supports), C1 to C14.

2When and who

Start this procedure in five cases:

  • We adopt it while we already use strategies. Each strategy in use is entered and listed within 60 (steps 3 to 10). None stops for lack of a listing.
  • You want to use a strategy that is not on the . A or another provider may also ask for one (steps 3 to 10).
  • A practitioner starts with us, or a new practice year begins (steps 14 to 17).
  • A plan is made, reviewed or changed (steps 12 and 13).
  • A date in the list below falls due.

The dates are:

  • at least every 3 months (step 19)
  • self-assessment within 60 business days of starting, then every 12 months (step 15)
  • peer review at least every 6 months (step 22)
  • the goals and hours check at 6 months (step 25)
  • the quarterly review of the strategy list, every 3 months (step 27).

Who acts:

  • The Service Manager names the and a deputy (step 1).
  • The Quality Manager lists the National Best Practice Framework for Early Childhood Intervention (2025) and reports on the whole team (steps 2 and 30).
  • The practitioner chooses a strategy within their professional scope, makes its entry and keeps their (steps 3 to 8, 14, 15, 17, 18, 21 and 23).
  • The Practice supervisor keeps the strategy list and signs off practitioners for health-related strategies (steps 9 to 11). They also review self-assessments, hold supervision, check plans and learning, review the list and act on concerns (steps 16, 19, 20 and 24 to 29).
  • The checks plans against the strategy list and explains the evidence to the family (steps 12 and 13).
  • The peer reviewer reviews a colleague's practice (step 22).

When we adopt this procedure, the Practice supervisor lists every strategy already in use within 5 business days and answers Q24 to Q26 for each one at once. A strategy that fails Q24 or the law stops that day. Every strategy in use has its entry and listing within 60 business days of adoption (our standard). No strategy stops for lack of an entry or a listing.

In a small provider one person may hold several roles. A sole trader is the practitioner, the plan lead, the Service Manager and the Quality Manager. A sole trader engages one outside clinical supervisor with early childhood experience as Practice supervisor, found through their professional body's supervision register or a peer network; a case discussion with that supervisor is the peer review. A sole trader lists their own entries, and the outside supervisor initials them at the quarterly review. A sole trader gives the year-end record and one strategy entry to the independent contact named in REG-GOV-01 Delegations Register every 12 months. A student or volunteer works only with a practitioner watching, and makes no entry alone.

3Before you start

  • The Practice supervisor, the deputy and the National Best Practice Framework for Early Childhood Intervention (2025) are named (steps 1 and 2).
  • You have read the six principles in POL-ECS-07 ground rule G2.
  • You have FRM-ECS-06 Practice Reflection and Professional Development Record. Open a blank one for a new practitioner or a new strategy.
  • For an , you have one or two sources, or you can say what practice wisdom and the family's preference support.
  • You have your qualification and registration details.
  • For a plan check, you have the child's plan, FRM-ECS-07 Child and Family Support Plan, and REG-ECS-01 Early Childhood Supports Register, column V.

4Watch out

  • A strategy with no entry. Nobody can say what it rests on, so nobody can tell the family honestly or see when the evidence changes.
  • Evidence from the seller. A claim from the maker or seller of a strategy can look strong and be wrong. The family may spend money and hope on it.
  • A strategy that restrains, secludes or confines a child. It can hurt the child and take away their rights. The NDIS rules regulate it strictly. No strategy of ours may do it.
  • Working outside your qualification. A strategy for eating, drinking, swallowing, medicine or any health procedure can seriously hurt a child. This is so when the person is not qualified for it.
  • Training taken for skill, in a health-related strategy. A course does not show that you can do the strategy. Without a , it may be delivered badly and hurt a child.
  • A rating with no example. A high rating that nobody checked hides a gap. The child then gets the gap.
  • A peer alone with a child, or a child named in a group. It puts the child at risk and breaches their privacy.
  • Reflection used to punish. If people fear it, they write what feels safe and not what is true. The record then stops showing real practice.

5Steps

Set up

Step 1

Service Manager

Name the Practice supervisor and a deputy.

Choose people with early childhood experience who can judge the evidence for the strategies we use. Nobody supervises a person who supervises them. If nobody inside can do it, engage one outside clinical supervisor in writing. The agreement covers confidentiality, the NDIS Code of Conduct, how they raise a concern and who owns the records. A sole trader engages the outside Practice supervisor. Add each person to REG-GOV-01 Delegations Register as the holder of the position.

Result
Every practitioner has a named Practice supervisor and a deputy who can decide.
Record
REG-GOV-01 (position holder)
Time limit
Before any practitioner sees a child. Within 10 business days when either person leaves (our standard)

Carries out: POL-ECS-07 C9.

Step 2

Quality Manager

List the National Best Practice Framework for Early Childhood Intervention (2025) as an outside document.

The Framework is the national best practice guidance for early childhood intervention. Add it, with its edition, to REG-GOV-03 Master Document Register as an outside document. Name the Practice supervisor as its owner. Write in the row that POL-ECS-07, PRO-ECS-07 and FRM-ECS-06 carry it. The monthly check under PRO-QMS-01 Quality Management Procedure tells you when a new edition comes out. Tell the Practice supervisor within 5 business days.

Result
Every practitioner works from one named framework, and we know when it was last checked.
Record
REG-GOV-03 (outside document row: title, edition, owner, documents that carry it)
Time limit
Before the first strategy is listed. Then checked every month (our standard)

Carries out: POL-ECS-07 C4, POL-ECS-07 C8.

Check a strategy before use

Step 3

Warning. A strategy with no entry may rest on nothing. The family cannot be told honestly what it rests on.

Practitioner

If you want to use a strategy that is not on the strategy list, or a family or another provider asks for one:

Describe the strategy and the change it should bring.

Open a new Section C in your FRM-ECS-06. Name the strategy. Say what it is for, which children it suits and which it does not, and where it would be used. Write what we would expect to see in the child's outcome levels if it works. If a family or another provider asked, tell the plan lead the same day, so the family knows we are checking it. Make the entry (steps 3 to 8) before you use the strategy with a child; it is short, and the strategy may be used from the day of the entry unless it fails Q24 or the law.

Result
The strategy is named, and its purpose and its measure are clear.
Record
FRM-ECS-06 Q17, Q18 and Q19
Time limit
Before the strategy is used with any child. For a family's request, start within 5 business days and give the family an answer within 20 business days (our standard)

Carries out: POL-ECS-07 C1. Written on: FRM-ECS-06 Q17, FRM-ECS-06 Q18, FRM-ECS-06 Q19.

Step 4

Practitioner

Check the strategy against our six principles.

Use the six principles in POL-ECS-07 ground rule G2, drawn from the National Best Practice Framework for Early Childhood Intervention (2025). Write which principles the strategy rests on and how. A no for principle 1 or 6 means the strategy is not used. For any other no, say how we will make up for it.

Result
The principles the strategy rests on are written down.
Record
FRM-ECS-06 Q20
Time limit
Before the strategy is used (our standard)

Carries out: POL-ECS-07 C1. Written on: FRM-ECS-06 Q20.

Step 5

Practitioner

Name one or two sources, or the practice wisdom and family preference the strategy draws on, and who gains from it.

Start with the Framework in REG-GOV-03, then a guideline, review, study or professional body statement. One or two sources are enough. Write where you found each one. Where there is no published source, write the practice wisdom it draws on (your discipline's accepted practice, a supervisor's or expert's advice) and the family's preference. If the maker or seller of the strategy wrote, funded or sold a source, find a second source with no link to them. A testimonial or a website alone is not a source. If you cannot reach a source, ask the expert you named at Q5.

Result
Every strategy names what it rests on.
Record
FRM-ECS-06 Q21
Time limit
Before the strategy is used (our standard)

Carries out: POL-ECS-07 C1. Written on: FRM-ECS-06 Q21.

Step 6

Practitioner

Write the in words.

At Q22 choose the basis that fits and write it in words, never as a letter: in a current framework or guideline; shown in a review or study; limited or early evidence, or evidence from other groups; practice wisdom and family preference with no harm signal; or shown to harm or not to work. Judge it for children like this one in age, need, language and culture. Then write what the sources say about risks, and about who the strategy does not suit, at Q23. A tool that was not tested with children of this age, language and culture is judged for the group it was tested with. A score is never the only basis for a decision. Decision table 1 shows what each basis allows.

Result
The evidence basis is written, with the reasons and the risks.
Record
FRM-ECS-06 Q22 and Q23
Time limit
Before the strategy is used (our standard)

Carries out: POL-ECS-07 C2. Written on: FRM-ECS-06 Q22, FRM-ECS-06 Q23.

Step 7

Warning. A strategy that restrains, secludes or confines a child, or a health procedure done by someone who is not qualified, can seriously hurt a child.

Practitioner

Check the law and the qualification the strategy needs.

Answer Q24 to Q27. At Q24, write yes if the primary purpose of the strategy is to manage or change the child's behaviour by restraining, secluding or confining the child, or by limiting what they can reach or use. Ordinary prompting the child accepts, a reflexive hold away from danger and safety equipment used for safety are not restraint; the Q24 hint lists them. If you are still not sure, write yes and ask. A yes means stop: tell the Service Manager the same day, and the strategy is not used. At Q25, say whether it is health-related and name the qualification it needs. At Q26, list any touch, recording, equipment, app or sharing, and the agreement it needs. At Q27, write the discipline or scope that covers it, whether a sign-off is needed, and any .

Result
The legal limits and the qualification needed are written down.
Record
FRM-ECS-06 Q24, Q25, Q26 and Q27
Time limit
Before the strategy is used. A yes at Q24 goes to the Service Manager the same day (our standard)

Carries out: POL-ECS-07 C3. Written on: FRM-ECS-06 Q24, FRM-ECS-06 Q25, FRM-ECS-06 Q26, FRM-ECS-06 Q27.

Step 8

Practitioner

Write what we will tell the family and others.

At Q28 write the in plain words. Say what the strategy is, what it asks of the family and what the evidence says, in words. Say how sure we are, what else they could choose (including no new strategy), and any risk or cost. For a , say that it is a trial and when we will look. At Q29 list each handout, picture guide or video we will give the family or others in the child's life.

Result
The family summary is ready, and each piece of information is listed for checking.
Record
FRM-ECS-06 Q28 and Q29
Time limit
Before the family is asked to agree to the support (our standard)

Carries out: POL-ECS-07 C5, POL-ECS-07 C6. Written on: FRM-ECS-06 Q28, FRM-ECS-06 Q29.

Step 9

Practice supervisor

Read the entry and add the strategy to the one-page strategy list, with any condition.

Read the whole of Section C. Check the restraint and law answers first. Open the main source where there is one. Check each handout at Q29 against the strategy, then write who checked it and the date. Use Decision table 1. Give the strategy its number and write at Q30 that it is listed, any condition (a limit, a measure, a review point), the reasons and the next quarterly review date. If the entry is thin, ask for a change: another source, a measure, a limit. You may list your own entry; a second clinician initials it at the quarterly review. Only where the practitioner and you disagree does the Service Manager decide, with an outside reviewer. The strategy may be used from the day of its entry; only a yes at Q24 or a breach of law stops it.

Result
The strategy is on the list, with any condition and its reasons.
Record
FRM-ECS-06 Q29 and Q30
Time limit
Within 10 business days of the entry (our standard)

Carries out: POL-ECS-07 C1, POL-ECS-07 C2, POL-ECS-07 C3, POL-ECS-07 C6. Written on: FRM-ECS-06 Q29, FRM-ECS-06 Q30.

Step 10

Practice supervisor

Tell the team and keep the list current.

The list holds, for each strategy, its number, name, principle, evidence basis, who may deliver it, any limit or role release, and its last review date. Keep the entry, the family summary and the handouts with the list. A strategy you have asked to stop stays on the list marked "stopped", with the reason, so nobody uses it again without new evidence. Tell every practitioner and plan lead what is on the list. Enter the health-related sign-offs, dates and hours in REG-HRM-02 Training and Competency Register; the list itself stays in the until a Rise strategy register exists.

Result
There is one list of strategies, and everyone who plans or delivers knows what is on it.
Record
FRM-ECS-06 Q30; the strategy list; REG-HRM-02
Time limit
Within 2 business days of listing (our standard)

Carries out: POL-ECS-07 C1. Written on: FRM-ECS-06 Q30.

Use a strategy with a child

Step 11

Warning. For a health-related strategy, a course does not show that a person can do it. A practitioner who has not been watched may deliver it badly.

Practice supervisor

Sign off each practitioner for each health-related strategy, and record any role release.

A registered or certified practitioner delivers strategies within their professional scope (Q3) without a separate sign-off. For a health-related strategy (eating, drinking, swallowing, medicine or a health procedure), sign off only when all three are true: the practitioner's qualification covers it (Q3 and Q27); any training named at Q27 is done and recorded under PRO-HRM-03 Training and Competency Procedure; a qualified practitioner has watched at least 2 sessions and judged them competent, using FRM-HRM-07 Training and Competency Assessment Record. Until then, write "learning" at Q6, and a qualified practitioner stays in the room. For role release, the qualified practitioner writes on the strategy list what is released, to whom, what they showed and the review interval; medicine and health procedures are never released. A sign-off does not lapse with time. Where a practitioner has not delivered the strategy for 6 months, talk it through at the next reflective supervision and decide together whether a watched session is needed.

Result
Only a qualified and signed-off practitioner delivers a health-related strategy on their own, and every other strategy is delivered within scope or under a written role release.
Record
FRM-ECS-06 Q6; the strategy list; REG-HRM-02
Time limit
Before the practitioner delivers a health-related strategy on their own (our standard)

Carries out: POL-ECS-07 C7. Written on: FRM-ECS-06 Q6.

Step 12

Plan lead

If a plan is made, reviewed or changed:

Check each support in the child's plan against the strategy list.

For each support at Q14 in FRM-ECS-07, find the strategy on the list and write its number on the support's line. The outcome's five-level scale at Q19 and Q20 is the only measure in the plan; do not add a separate strategy measure. If the strategy is not on the list, the support may stay in the plan: ask the practitioner to make the entry at step 3 before the plan is approved. If the strategy is health-related and nobody is signed off for it, tell the Service Manager and the family the same day. With the family's consent, refer them to a qualified provider or ask the expert named at Q5 for advice. Nobody delivers a health-related strategy until someone is signed off.

Result
Every support in a plan carries a strategy number, and every health-related strategy has a signed-off practitioner.
Record
FRM-ECS-07 Q14
Time limit
Before the plan is approved or changed (our standard)

Carries out: POL-ECS-07 C1, POL-ECS-07 C7. Written on: FRM-ECS-07 Q14, FRM-ECS-07 Q21.

Step 13

Plan lead

Explain the evidence and the choices to the family.

Use the family summary from Q28, in the way the family communicates. Say how sure we are, what the strategy asks of them, what else they could choose, and any risk or cost. Ask what they think, and give them time. Write the date and their decision (agreed, declined or trial) on the support's line at Q14 of FRM-ECS-07. A part they declined is not carried out. For a monitored trial, say that it is a trial and when we will look again. If the family wants to read the sources, give them the list at Q21. A family may say no to any strategy. Saying no never reduces supports. If the family asked for a strategy we do not use because it is shown to harm or not to work, explain why and that they may use it themselves. If it could harm the child, tell the the same day.

Result
The family has heard the evidence honestly, and their decision is written down.
Record
FRM-ECS-07 Q14
Time limit
Before the family says the plan or the change is theirs (our standard)

Carries out: POL-ECS-07 C5. Written on: FRM-ECS-07 Q23.

Keep your practice current

Step 14

Practitioner

Open your practice record.

Open FRM-ECS-06 on your first day, and the next record the day the last one closes. Complete Q1 to Q5. Say what you are qualified to do and what you do not do. Book at least 4 reflective supervisions, no more than 3 months apart. List the sources you can reach and who you can ask. If you cannot reach a source or an expert, tell the Practice supervisor within 5 business days. Give the Service Manager your qualification and registration details. The Service Manager checks them with the body and writes the date at Q2.

Result
The record is open, with your limits, your supervision dates and your sources.
Record
FRM-ECS-06 Q1 to Q5
Time limit
Within 5 business days of starting, then each 12 months (our standard)

Carries out: POL-ECS-07 C8. Written on: FRM-ECS-06 Q1, FRM-ECS-06 Q2, FRM-ECS-06 Q3, FRM-ECS-06 Q4, FRM-ECS-06 Q5.

Step 15

Practitioner

Complete your self-assessment.

Rate yourself 1 to 4 on each of the eight domains at Q7 to Q14. For each rating give one example from a record in the last 6 months, with the record number and date. A new starter may use an example from a previous role, with no child's name. A rating with no example is not accepted. Write one thing you will do next. Be honest. Nobody is disciplined for a low rating.

Result
There is a rated self-assessment with an example for each domain.
Record
FRM-ECS-06 Q7 to Q14
Time limit
Within 60 business days of starting, then every 12 months (our standard)

Carries out: POL-ECS-07 C10. Written on: FRM-ECS-06 Q7, FRM-ECS-06 Q8, FRM-ECS-06 Q9, FRM-ECS-06 Q10, FRM-ECS-06 Q11, FRM-ECS-06 Q12, FRM-ECS-06 Q13, FRM-ECS-06 Q14.

Step 16

Practice supervisor

Review the self-assessment with the practitioner.

Read the record behind each example for a rating of 1 or 4, and at least one other. Write where you agree and where you see it differently, and why. The practitioner may add their view. Use Decision table 2. Agree up to 3 goals that the practitioner can check.

Result
The self-assessment is checked, and the practitioner has up to 3 goals.
Record
FRM-ECS-06 Q15 and Q16
Time limit
Within 10 business days of the self-assessment (our standard)

Carries out: POL-ECS-07 C10. Written on: FRM-ECS-06 Q15, FRM-ECS-06 Q16.

Step 17

Practitioner

Write your plan.

Build the plan from your goals, peer feedback, new evidence and what families told you. Plan the hours your professional standard sets, and at least 20 hours in the 12 months, pro rata for part-time hours, where your profession sets none. At least half must be on early childhood intervention practice or the evidence behind our strategies. Count supervision and peer review time only where your professional standard counts it. Say who pays and who allows the time. The Practice supervisor checks the hours and agrees the plan at Q43. The Service Manager agrees the time and the cost.

Result
There is a dated learning plan that meets our standard.
Record
FRM-ECS-06 Q42 and Q43
Time limit
Within 10 business days of agreeing the goals at step 16 (our standard)

Carries out: POL-ECS-07 C12. Written on: FRM-ECS-06 Q42, FRM-ECS-06 Q43.

Step 18

Practitioner

Write your reflection before each reflective supervision.

Read your session records, FRM-ECS-05 questions 28 and 30. Pick two sessions: one that went well and one that did not. Write what you learned, what you will keep and what you will change. Say what happened to the change you agreed last time. Use record numbers and never a child's name.

Result
You come to supervision with real examples and one change in mind.
Record
FRM-ECS-06 Q33
Time limit
Before each reflective supervision (our standard)

Carries out: POL-ECS-07 C9. Written on: FRM-ECS-06 Q33.

Step 19

Practice supervisor

Hold reflective supervision.

Read the reflection first. Ask what the practitioner noticed, and not only what they did. Talk about the strategies they use: do they still trust the evidence, and what questions have come up? Cover their goals and their learning. Agree one change and who will check it. Write the date and who took part. A meeting about workload or wellbeing under PRO-HRM-02 Supervision and Performance Procedure may be held at the same time, but it is recorded there.

Result
The practitioner has reflected with a second person and has one agreed change.
Record
FRM-ECS-06 Q32 and Q36
Time limit
At least every 3 months (our standard)

Carries out: POL-ECS-07 C9. Written on: FRM-ECS-06 Q32, FRM-ECS-06 Q36.

Step 20

Practice supervisor

Check two of the practitioner's plans and their outcomes, in the quarterly read.

This is part of the one quarterly read, with the session records under PRO-ECS-06 and the strategy list (step 27). Pick one plan at random, and ask the practitioner to pick one. For each support, check the strategy number, that it is on the list, that the practitioner works within scope or is signed off for a health-related strategy, and that the family's decision is recorded at Q14. Then read REG-ECS-01 column V for the same children. Look for an outcome that shows "no change" or "gone back" at two reviews. Ask whether the strategy fits the child and whether it was used as listed. Ask what the outcome levels show. If the strategy needs a change, note it for step 27 and tell the plan lead. Give each gap an owner and a date.

Result
Practice has been checked against real plans and real outcomes.
Record
FRM-ECS-06 Q34 and Q35
Time limit
At each reflective supervision, at least every 3 months (our standard)

Carries out: POL-ECS-07 C13. Written on: FRM-ECS-06 Q34, FRM-ECS-06 Q35.

Step 21

Practitioner

Arrange a peer review.

Choose a peer who knows early childhood practice and has no line of authority over you. Check there is no conflict. A sole trader uses a case discussion with the outside clinical supervisor. If the peer will watch a session, ask the family first, in the way they communicate, and write their words. The family may say no, and then you choose another kind of review. The peer's own organisation's clearance covers them: ask for their working with children check details as the law of [state or territory] requires (check the schedule in POL-CHS-01 Child Safe Policy) and a short visitor acknowledgement of our child safe code. A parent, carer or educator stays in the room. The peer is never alone with the child.

Result
A peer is chosen, the family has agreed, and the peer is cleared.
Time limit
Before the review day (our standard)

Carries out: POL-ECS-07 C11. Written on: FRM-ECS-06 Q37, FRM-ECS-06 Q39.

Step 22

Peer reviewer

Give the practitioner feedback on their practice.

Watch one session, or read two session records, or talk through a case by phone with no names. Use the eight domains at Q7 to Q14 as your guide. Keep what you see confidential. Tell the practitioner what they did well, what you ask them to think about, and what you suggest they try. Ask for their reply. Write it at Q40 and read it back. If you saw anything unsafe, or a health-related strategy delivered outside a sign-off, or a strategy with no entry, tell the Practice supervisor the same day. If you saw a child at , tell the child safety lead the same day.

Result
The practitioner has feedback they can use and one thing to try.
Record
FRM-ECS-06 Q38, Q40 and Q41
Time limit
At least every 6 months. Feedback within 5 business days of the review (our standard)

Carries out: POL-ECS-07 C11. Written on: FRM-ECS-06 Q38, FRM-ECS-06 Q40, FRM-ECS-06 Q41.

Step 23

Practitioner

Record each professional development activity.

Add a line for each activity. Write the date, what it was, who ran it and the hours. Write where the certificate or your notes are kept, what you learned and what you will change. Count only the time spent learning. Reading counts when you keep notes.

Result
Your learning is on record.
Record
FRM-ECS-06 Q44
Time limit
Within 5 business days of the activity (our standard)

Carries out: POL-ECS-07 C12. Written on: FRM-ECS-06 Q44.

Step 24

Practice supervisor

Check what changed after each activity.

For an activity of 3 hours or more, ask at the reflective supervision 3 months later what the practitioner now does differently. Ask for one example by record number. Read that record. Write whether you see the change. If you do not yet see it, agree the next action and add it to the goals.

Result
Learning is judged by what changes in practice.
Record
FRM-ECS-06 Q45
Time limit
Within 3 months of the activity (our standard)

Carries out: POL-ECS-07 C12. Written on: FRM-ECS-06 Q45.

Step 25

Practice supervisor

Check the goals and the hours at 6 months.

Compare each goal and the hours done with the plan. If the practitioner is behind, agree dated catch-up steps. If a goal needs more support, tell the Service Manager.

Result
A shortfall is found while there is time to fix it.
Record
FRM-ECS-06 Q46
Time limit
At 6 months of each practice year (our standard)

Carries out: POL-ECS-07 C10, POL-ECS-07 C12. Written on: FRM-ECS-06 Q46.

Step 26

Practice supervisor

Close the practice year.

Count from the record against the standard at Q47. Write each gap with an owner and a date. Enter the totals in REG-HRM-02. If the standard was not met, tell the Service Manager. Open the next record and carry over the goals at Q48.

Result
The year is closed, the record is complete and the next one is open.
Record
FRM-ECS-06 Q47 and Q48
Time limit
Within 10 business days of the end of the practice year (our standard)

Carries out: POL-ECS-07 C12. Written on: FRM-ECS-06 Q47, FRM-ECS-06 Q48.

Keep strategies current

Step 27

Practice supervisor

Review the strategy list every 3 months.

Read the list. For each strategy, look for new evidence, practice alerts and changes to the Framework in REG-GOV-03. Read the outcomes of the children who use it (Q35). Ask for a change where needed: another source, a limit, a measure, or that it stops. Initial any entry the Practice supervisor made themselves. Write the result at Q31 and on the list. Check that the family summary and each handout still match. Set the next review date.

Result
Each listing is current, or has been changed.
Record
FRM-ECS-06 Q31
Time limit
Every 3 months. A monitored trial is also looked at at the next progress check of each child who uses it (our standard)

Carries out: POL-ECS-07 C4. Written on: FRM-ECS-06 Q31.

Step 28

Practice supervisor

If a worker, a family, the Framework or a regulator brings new evidence, a practice alert or a notice about a strategy on the list:

Act on the new evidence.

Any worker who learns of it tells the Practice supervisor within 2 business days. Use Decision table 3. Give each plan lead the record numbers of the children whose plans use the strategy. Plan leads tell each family and change the plans. Raise an improvement request on FRM-QMS-01 Improvement / Corrective Action Request Form with the source "practice alert or new evidence". The Quality Manager adds the entry under PRO-QMS-01 Quality Management Procedure.

Result
The change reaches every child and family it affects.
Record
FRM-ECS-06 Q31; FRM-QMS-01; REG-QMS-01
Time limit
As Decision table 3 sets (our standard)

Carries out: POL-ECS-07 C4. Written on: FRM-ECS-06 Q9, FRM-ECS-06 Q31.

Step 29

Practice supervisor

If a worker reports, or a record shows, that a strategy was used that fails the restraint or law questions, or that someone delivered a health-related strategy outside their qualification or sign-off, or that a strategy in use has no entry:

Act on the concern.

For a strategy that fails Q24 or the law, or a health-related strategy delivered outside a sign-off, stop the use the same day and then look into it. Tell the Service Manager. Talk to the practitioner first, then find which children were affected. If a child may have been hurt, follow PRO-INC-01 Incident Management Procedure. For a strategy with no entry, ask the practitioner to make the entry at step 3 within 10 business days; it need not stop unless it fails Q24 or the law. If the problem is scope, decide at step 11. Raise an improvement request on FRM-QMS-01 Improvement / Corrective Action Request Form. The Quality Manager adds the entry. Nobody is disadvantaged for raising a concern.

Result
Any unsafe or unlawful use has stopped, every strategy has its entry, and the cause is found and fixed.
Record
FRM-QMS-01; REG-QMS-01
Time limit
Stop an unsafe or unlawful use the same day. Look into it within 5 business days (our standard)

Carries out: POL-ECS-07 C14.

Step 30

Quality Manager

Report the results for the whole team to the governing body.

Count the strategies on the list, on monitored trial, stopped and overdue for review. Count self-assessments, reflective supervisions, peer reviews and learning hours against the standard. Read the themes at Q33 and the concerns raised at step 29. Read the full records of two practitioners. Raise each theme that touches more than one practitioner in REG-QMS-01. Report in the one 6 monthly early childhood quality report to the governing body covering sections 56 to 62. A sole trader reports to the independent contact.

Result
Practice across the whole team is checked, and each weakness becomes an action.
Record
REG-QMS-01
Time limit
Every 6 months (our standard)

Carries out: POL-ECS-07 C13.

6Decision

7If it goes wrong

  • The Practice supervisor is away for more than 10 business days. The deputy decides, signs off and holds supervision. A sole trader's outside Practice supervisor names an outside deputy.
  • The listing will take longer than 10 business days. Tell the practitioner before the day. Write the new date and the reason. The strategy may be used meanwhile unless it fails Q24 or the law. Never change a date to hide a late one.
  • A family asks for a strategy shown to harm or not to work. Explain honestly, as step 13 sets out. The family decides what to try outside our supports. We keep supporting the rest of the plan and never reduce it. If the strategy could harm the child, tell the child safety lead the same day.
  • Another provider asks us to coach a strategy of theirs. Check it the same way, using the sources that provider gives us. Do this only with the family's consent. If we cannot check it, we do not coach it. Tell the family and the other provider, and ask the family what they want.
  • The only practitioner signed off for a health-related strategy is away. A practitioner who is not signed off does not deliver it on their own. The plan lead follows the continuity arrangement in REG-ECS-01 column Y and tells the family the same day.
  • Nobody we can reach has the expertise a child needs. Tell the plan lead and the Service Manager the same day. The plan lead tells the family. With their consent, refer them to a qualified provider, or ask the named expert for advice. Nobody delivers a health-related strategy until a signed-off practitioner is available.
  • A practitioner disagrees with a listing, a condition, a rating or a review. Write their view in the record. They may ask the Service Manager for a second look within 5 business days. The Service Manager decides with an outside reviewer.
  • A self-assessment, a plan or a peer review is overdue. The practitioner tells the Practice supervisor before the date. They write a new date and the reason. If it is 20 business days late, the Service Manager asks what is in the way: time, workload, fear or something else. Nobody is disciplined for reflecting honestly.
  • No peer is available. In a small or remote team, ask an outside peer by phone or video. Use a records review or a case discussion with no names. Do not record video of a child.
  • The family says no to a peer watching. Use another kind of review. Supports do not change.
  • A strategy is in use with no entry. Make the entry at step 3 within 10 business days. It stops only if it fails Q24 or the law (step 29).
  • You are worried about a colleague's practice. Tell the Practice supervisor the same day. If your worry is about a colleague's conduct towards a child or family, about safety, or about the Practice supervisor, tell the Chief Executive. If it is about the Chief Executive, tell the chair of the governing body. A sole trader's concern goes to the independent contact named in REG-GOV-01. This is the one rule POL-ECS-01 Early Childhood Supports Policy sets.
  • You think a child is at risk of harm. Do not wait for this procedure. Follow PRO-ECS-02 The Child Procedure (Early Childhood Supports) and tell the child safety lead the same day.
  • The system is down. Complete the paper form the same day. Enter it in the system within 1 business day of it coming back.

8Done means

  • Every strategy in use is on the strategy list with its number, principle, evidence basis, who may deliver it and any limit.
  • A strategy the Practice supervisor stopped is on the list with its reason.
  • Every support in every plan carries a strategy number, and every family's decision is recorded on the support's line.
  • Each practitioner is signed off for each health-related strategy they deliver on their own, and any role release is written on the list.
  • Each practitioner has a practice record for the year with a self-assessment, supervision dates, peer reviews and a learning plan.
  • Each learning activity is recorded, and each larger one has a check of what changed.
  • Each concern about a strategy that fails the restraint or law questions, or health-related practice outside a sign-off, has an entry in REG-QMS-01.
  • REG-HRM-02 shows the dates, the hours and the health-related sign-offs.

9Quick card

131 words
  • Make the short entry before you use a strategy that is not on the strategy list (step 3).
  • Stop at once any strategy that restrains, secludes or confines a child (step 7).
  • Do only what your professional scope covers. A health-related strategy needs a sign-off (step 11).
  • Tell the family what the evidence says before they agree (step 13).
  • Write the evidence basis in words, from the sources and not from the seller (step 6).
  • Tell the Practice supervisor the same day about a strategy that fails the restraint or law questions, or health-related practice outside a sign-off (step 29).
  • Hold reflective supervision at least every 3 months (step 19).
  • Have a peer review at least every 6 months (step 22).
  • Record each learning activity within 5 business days (step 23).

form.intro:
This is the . It is one practitioner's record of how their practice stays evidence-informed for 12 months. It holds their qualifications and scope, their self-assessment, the short for each strategy they bring in, their reflections, their peer reviews and their .

Keep one practice record for each practitioner. A record covers one practice year of 12 months. Open the next record the day this one closes. Add dated entries as things happen. Never write over an old entry. The Practice supervisor keeps each practitioner's : the record and what supports it.

When | Complete these questions

When you start, and each new practice year: questions 1 to 5, then 7 to 14 within 60 business days (12 months for a later year).

Before you first use a strategy that is not on the strategy list: Section C, questions 17 to 29 (a short entry). The Practice supervisor lists it at question 30.

Each reflective supervision, every 3 months: questions 32 to 36.

Each peer review, every 6 months: questions 37 to 41.

Each learning activity: question 44; question 45 three months later for an activity of 3 hours or more.

At 6 months: question 46. At year end: Section G.

This record is in practice a set of five records (profile, self-assessment, supervision log, peer review, learning log) kept under one number; splitting it is a 0.4.0 item.

Who completes it:

  • The practitioner completes questions 1 to 5, 7 to 14, 33, 37, 39, 42, 44 and 46, and the first part of question 45, as each event happens. The practitioner also completes questions 17 to 29 for each strategy they bring in that is not yet on the strategy list.
  • The Practice supervisor completes question 6, questions 15 and 16 and question 30 (the listing). They also complete question 31, questions 32 and 34 to 36, question 43, the view in question 45 and Section G.
  • The peer reviewer completes questions 38, 40 and 41.
  • The Service Manager, with an outside reviewer, decides question 30 only where the practitioner and the Practice supervisor disagree.

Complete Section C once for each strategy, before you first use it with a child. A strategy is any approach, programme, technique, assessment tool, outcome measure or piece of equipment that we use or recommend. The entry is short: one or two sources, or the practice wisdom and family preference the strategy draws on. The strategy may be used from the day of the entry unless question 24 is "yes" or the law bars it.

Have these ready:

  • the National Best Practice Framework for Early Childhood Intervention (2025), listed in REG-GOV-03 Master Document Register, and the sources you rely on
  • your session records, FRM-ECS-05 Coaching Session Record, especially questions 28 and 30
  • the plans of the children you work with, FRM-ECS-07 Child and Family Support Plan
  • the outcomes in REG-ECS-01 Early Childhood Supports Register, column V
  • your qualification and registration details
  • last year's practice record, if there is one.

Never write a child's name on this record. Use the child's record number from REG-ECS-01 column A. If you do not know an answer, write "not yet known" and the date. Ask your Practice supervisor.

What happens next: the Practice supervisor lists each strategy within 10 business days of its entry, and enters the dates, the hours and each health-related sign-off in REG-HRM-02 Training and Competency Register within 2 business days. PRO-ECS-07 Evidence-Informed Practice Procedure (Early Childhood Supports) sets every step.
form.privacy:
Say this to each practitioner when you open their record.

"We write down your qualifications, your self-assessment, your reflections, your peer reviews and your learning. We do this to help you grow, and to show that the strategies we use are backed by evidence. The law requires us to show that our workers are competent for their role.

Your Practice supervisor reads this record. So do the Service Manager and the Quality Manager. A peer reviewer reads the part about the review they do. An auditor may read it.

We use it for learning. A rating or a reflection is never, by itself, a reason to discipline you. We must act if a record shows a child may be at risk, or that someone worked outside their qualification.

We never put a child's name on this record. If a child's information is needed, we use their record number.

You can read your record and ask us to correct it. Ask [privacy contact role and contact details]."

[Provider name] handles this record under the Privacy Act 1988 (Cth) and POL-INF-01 Information Management Policy. If you are a contractor, student or volunteer, the Australian Privacy Principles apply to this record.

form.intro:
This is the support plan for one child and their family. It says what will change in the child's and the family's daily life. It also says what each person will do to help, and how we will know it is working. The family keeps a copy. Every worker who sees the child follows it.

The plan is made of . Each one is something the child or the family will do in a routine, a place and with people, which anyone could see or hear. Each outcome has supports, which the Quality Indicators call interventions, and a way of measuring.

Keep one plan for each child. Version 0 is the interim plan: one to three starting outcomes and their supports, agreed with the family within 10 business days of the first session, with no five-level scale and no Service Manager approval. starts under it. Version 1 is the first full plan and replaces it. A new version is made whenever an outcome, a measure or a support changes. The last approved version stays in force until the new one is approved.

Who completes it:

  • The completes every section except Section B and questions 24 and 25, with the family, at a time and place the family chooses. Where the plan lead asks a practitioner to write a part, the plan lead stays accountable.
  • A parent or carer can write their own answers instead. The family can bring anyone: an interpreter, an advocate or a cultural support person.
  • The practitioner who assesses the child completes Section B. For FRM-ECS-03 that is the plan lead.
  • The Service Manager completes questions 24 and 25.

Have ready:

  • the family record, FRM-ECS-02 Family Strengths, Needs and Priorities Record
  • the assessment, FRM-ECS-03 Everyday Routines and Participation Assessment, and any other assessment report
  • the team record, FRM-ECS-04 Team Around the Child Record, for who may see what
  • the family's communication preferences, on FRM-RGT-01 Communication, Advocacy and Support Preferences Form
  • the child's row in REG-ECS-01 Early Childhood Supports Register
  • for a check or review, the last approved version and the FRM-ECS-05 Coaching Session Record entries for the plan period
  • an interpreter, if the family wants one.

Where the provider has adopted PRO-SUP-02 Support Planning Procedure and FRM-SUP-02 Participant Support Plan Template, this plan is the child's support plan under them, and the FRM-SUP-02 sections that hold the critical summary, consent, risks, emergencies and who has the plan are attached; where FRM-SUP-02 asks what this plan also asks, answer it here and write "see FRM-ECS-07 question" and its number there. Until a Rise version exists, question 18 holds the critical information, emergency steps, risks and who holds the plan. This plan does not authorise any restraint, seclusion or other restrictive practice.

What happens next: PRO-ECS-08 Outcome Based Approach Procedure (Early Childhood Supports) sets every step. The family gets their copy within 5 business days of approval: the page "Our plan in our words" at the end of this form, one page per outcome, in the language and format they chose. We check each outcome with the family every 3 months and review the plan at least every 6 months.
form.privacy:
This statement is for the family. Read it aloud, in the language and way the family uses.

"We write this plan with you. It says what you want for your child and your family, what each of us will do, and how we will know it is working. We use your words where we can.

You choose what goes in the plan. You can say no to any question and to any part of the plan. Saying no does not reduce your child's supports.

The workers who support your child read this plan. So do the Service Manager and the Quality Manager. We give the plan to a teacher, an educator or another service only if you agree, and only the parts you agree to.

We write down how your child is going and use it to show you. We do not use it to judge you or your family.

There is one exception. The law may require us to share information without your consent to keep a child safe. PRO-ECS-02 The Child Procedure (Early Childhood Supports) sets whether and when we tell you, following the advice of the child protection agency of [state or territory].

You can read this plan, ask for a copy in the way that suits you, and ask us to correct it at any time. Ask [privacy contact role and contact details]."

Tell an educator or another provider who adds to this plan that the family will read what they say.

[Provider name] holds this plan under the Privacy Act 1988 (Cth) and POL-INF-01 Information Management Policy.
form.after:
• Service Manager: approve the plan, or return it with the reasons, within 5 business days of the family agreeing (step 16, our standard). The interim plan (version 0) needs no approval.
  • Plan lead: enter the approved plan in REG-ECS-01 within 2 business days of approval (step 17, our standard).
  • Plan lead: give the family their copy within 5 business days of approval. Ask them to say it back (steps 18 and 19, our standard).
  • Plan lead: give the plan to each of our workers who sees the child before their next contact (step 20, our standard).
  • Plan lead: hold a progress check at least every 3 months. Enter it in REG-ECS-01 within 2 business days (steps 22 and 24, our standard).
  • Plan lead: give the family a progress report at each plan review, and at least every 6 months (step 25, our standard).
  • A person with parental responsibility can ask for a copy of any record about their child. We give it within 10 business days (our standard).
  • The plan is filed in the child's file. Keep it for 7 years after supports end (NDIS Act 2013, section 45B, from 27 August 2026), or until the child turns 25, whichever is later (our standard). Check the law of [state or territory] before a child's record is destroyed. Some laws set a longer time.

columns.from: The plan lead, when the row is opened under PRO-ECS-01

columns.name: Child
columns.meaning: Who the row is about

register.proves:
This register holds one row for every child who receives from [Provider name]. The row is the index to the child's file. It shows who the is, who is in the team, what the family agreed to, and when each plan, review and report was due and done.

  • Indicators evidenced: s 56 (1) to s 56 (4), s 56 (5)(a) and s 56 (5)(b).
  • Also s 57 (1) to s 57 (8), on the family.
  • Also s 58 (1) to s 58 (4), on inclusion, and s 59 (1) to s 59 (4), on collaboration.
  • Also s 60 (1) to s 60 (5), on capacity building, and s 61 (2), on skills.
  • Also s 62 (1) to s 62 (6), on outcomes.
  • Legal basis: National Disability Insurance Scheme (Provider Registration and Practice Standards) Rules 2018, Schedule 5, clauses 3 to 9. Section 20(3), item 18 of those Rules applies Schedules 1 and 5 to early intervention supports for early childhood.
  • No NDIS instrument sets the columns of this register. The columns are our standard, built from the indicators.
  • Each fact is held once. The forms hold the detail and the family's words. This register holds the dates, the names, the counts, the record numbers and a one-line pointer to the form.
  • Clearances and training are in REG-HRM-01 Worker Screening Register and REG-HRM-02 Training and Competency Register. Intake and the service agreement are in REG-SUP-01 Participant and Service Agreement Register (Rise version not yet written); until it exists, column F holds who has .
  • Retention: keep each row for 7 years after supports end, or until the child turns 25, whichever is later (our standard; NDIS Act 2013, section 45B (from 27 August 2026): records of claims and supports are kept for 7 years).
  • Retention where column J holds a record number: keep the row for 45 years (Royal Commission into Institutional Responses to Child Sexual Abuse, recommendation 8.1; our standard). Check the child safe and records law of [state or territory] at adoption and before any row is destroyed.

Columns A to G and I are filled before the first session, and columns H and Y by the end of it. Column J stays blank until a record exists. Columns K to X and AH are filled as the plan is made and followed. Columns Z, AA and AD are filled when an interruption, a transition or an exit comes up. Columns AB, AC, AE, AF, AG, AI, AJ, AK and AL are kept current for every row.
register.entry:
1. The opens the row within 2 of the family accepting our offer (our standard). The Service Manager names the plan lead that day.
  2. Use one row for each child. Brothers and sisters each get their own row, linked in column AF.
  3. Fill columns A to G and I before the first session. Column J stays blank until a record exists. The first session does not go ahead while column I is empty for the type of setting it is in.
  4. Fill columns H and Y by the end of the first session.
  5. Fill every other column within 2 business days of the form or meeting that produces it (our standard).
  6. Write "not yet asked" with a date when a required answer is not known. Ask at the next contact with the family.
  7. Never overwrite or delete an entry. A correction is a new version of the row, with the date, your name and the reason.
  8. Columns H, N, R, X, Z, AH, AI, AJ and AK hold dated entries. Add each new entry underneath the last one. Column AL holds one date, replaced at each check.
  9. The family's own words stay in the forms (FRM-ECS-02, FRM-ECS-03, FRM-ECS-05). This register holds dates, names, counts, record numbers and one-line pointers. Where a short phrase of the family's is entered, such as "none wanted" in column N, it is entered as it was said, signed or shown. Nobody tidies it.
  10. Column J takes record numbers only. Never write what was seen, said or suspected in this register.
  11. When the plan lead is away for more than 5 business days, the Service Manager names another worker to keep the row.
  12. When the system is down, complete the paper forms. Enter the row within 1 business day of the system coming back.
  13. A sole trader is the plan lead and keeps every row.

A row is closed only when all of these are true:

  • column AD is filled and column AC says "exited"
  • the family has their final progress report and their copy of the last plan
  • column AA shows the handover was given, or the family's decision that none was wanted
  • every consent line in column Q has a withdrawn date or an end date
  • nothing in column AE, AI, AJ, AK or AL is still due.
